scope: Proposition B.1 (Complete far-source estimate) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 129. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each commuted equation on such a finite slab, the sum of its budgets (A.17), together with its mixed charges (A.18), is bounded, for some fixed c1 > 0, by oR0→∞(1)(F + Sa) + C ∑ prior Fprior + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c1 ). (B.6) The finite prior order is: level P before the two h hierarchies; within each level lower total order first, then more laboratory times at equal total order, then fewer dilations S. Equal-index norms are aggregated. The constants on prior far quantities are independent of both matching radii. Small radial gains and nonlinear bootstrap products may cross this order. After fixed finite hierarchical weighting, Proposition A.6 therefore gives, for some c2 > 0, F ≤ oR0→∞(1)(F + Sa) + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c2 ). (B.7) The initial and starting-annulus correction costs satisfy the same bound. In particular the pure acceleration defect on the starting annulus has its direct small radial coefficient on Sa.
